title: Missing time: waking up by a reservoir dam near Newell
place_text: Reservoir dam near Newell, South Dakota

tellings.quote: The truck is parked behind the wall of a reservoir dam near a town called Newell, more than 8 miles from their post.
I put the mike down and stepped out of the vehicle only to find that we were somewhere other than at November-5.
The sun was just coming up and I could see that it was a dam that held water in a reservoir. It turned out to be located north of Newell, and is called Newell Lake, quite a few miles from the LF.
During debriefing, I was told that nearly four hours had passed and that six security police back-up Alert teams had been searching for us.

plain: In 1977, two Air Force security policemen guarding a nuclear missile site in South Dakota say they lost nearly four hours. They found their truck parked behind the wall of a reservoir dam near the town of Newell, more than 8 miles from their post. Michels tells the story on an episode where two veterans, Mario Woods and Michael Johnson, meet again decades later. The fullest account is an article by the journalist Robert Hastings, published on 10 September 2017 under the title "Former USAF Missile Security Policeman Tells of Apparent UFO Abduction at ICBM Site". An ICBM is a long-range nuclear missile. In it the former policeman says: "I put the mike down and stepped out of the vehicle only to find that we were somewhere other than at November-5," the launch site they had been sent to. He says the sun was coming up and he could see "a dam that held water in a reservoir", which turned out to be Newell Lake, "quite a few miles" away. At the debriefing, he says, he was told "that nearly four hours had passed and that six security police back-up Alert teams had been searching for us." UFO researchers call a gap like this "missing time", a span a person cannot remember. If the account is true, men guarding nuclear weapons were taken off their post without knowing how.
